questions.q: The vector $\overset{→}{a} = - \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ is rotated through a right angle, passing through the $y$-axis in its way and the resulting vector is $\overset{→}{b}$. Then the projection of $3\overset{→}{a} + \sqrt{2}\overset{→}{b}$ on $\overset{→}{c} = 5\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

The vector $\overset{→}{a} = - \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ is rotated through a right angle, passing through the $y$-axis in its way and the resulting vector is $\overset{→}{b}$

Now taking,~$\overset{→}{b} = \lambda\overset{→}{a} \times \left(\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{^}{j}\right)~{note here we have taken cross vector with $\overset{^}{j}$~as it is rotated along $y -$axis}

$⇒ \overset{→}{b} = \lambda \left(- \overset{^}{i} +$2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$\times \left( \left(- \overset{^}{i} +$2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)\times \overset{^}{j}\right)$

$⇒ \overset{→}{b} = \$lambda \left(- \overset{^}{i} +2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)\times \left(- \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{k}\right)$

$⇒ \overset{→}{b} = \lambda\left|$\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} \text{ and } \overset{^}{j} \text{ and } \overset{^}{k} \\ - 1 \text{ and } 2 \text{ and } 1 \\ - 1 \text{ and } 0 \text{ and } - 1\end{cases}$\right|$

$⇒ \overset{→}{b} = \lambda \left(-2\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right)$

Also magnitude of both vector will be equal,

So,\left|\overset{→}{b}\right| = \left|\overset{→}{a}\right|⇒ $\sqrt{6} = \sqrt{12}\left|\lambda\right|

$⇒ \lambda = \pm $\dfrac{1}{2}

(Now~$\lambda = $\dfrac{1}{2}rejected $∵ \overset{→}{b}$ makes acute angle with y axis )

So,~$\overset{→}{b} = - $\sqrt{2} \left(- \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$

Now projection of $3\overset{→}{a} + \sqrt{2}\overset{→}{b}$~on~$\overset{→}{c}$~is given by,

\left(3\overset{→}{a} + \sqrt{2b}\right) \cdot \overset{→}{c}\left|\overset{→}{c}\right| =$=3\sqrt{2}

$

questions.q: Let the position vectors of the points $A, B, C$ and $D$ be $5\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j} + 2\lambda\overset{^}{k}, \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}, - 2\overset{^}{i} + \lambda\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$ and~$- \overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k} .$ Let the set $S = { \lambda \in \mathbb{R}:$ the points $A, B, C$ and $D$ are coplanar} .$ The~$\mathop{∑}_{\lambda \in S} ( \lambda + 2{)}^{2}& is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given that:

$A ( 5, 5, 2\lambda )$,~$B \left(1, 2, 3\right)$,~$C \left(-2, \lambda, 4\right)$~and~

$D \left(-1, 5, 6\right)$.

Now,

$\overset{→}{AB} ≡ ( - 4, - 3, 3 - 2\lambda )$

$\overset{→}{AC} ≡ ( - 7, \lambda - 5, 4 - 2\lambda )$

$\overset{→}{AD} ≡ ( - 6, 0, 6 - 2\lambda )$

Given that~$A, B, C\text{and}D$~are coplanar.

$∴ [ \overset{→}{AB}\overset{→}{AC}\overset{→}{AD} ] = 0$

$⇒ \left|$\begin{cases}-4 & - 3 & 3 - 2\lambda \\ - 7 & \lambda - 5 & 4 - 2\lambda \\ - 6 & 0 & 6 - 2\lambda\end{cases}\right| = 0$

Expand the determinant along the first row.

$⇒ - 4\left[ \left(\lambda -$5\right)\left($6 - 2\lambda\right) - 0\right] - \left(-$3\right)\left[-$7 \left(6 - 2\lambda\right) - \left(-6\right)\left($4 - 2\lambda\right)\right] + \left(3 - 2\lambda\right) \left[0 - \left(-6\right)\left(\lambda -$5\right)\right]$

On solving the above equation we get,

$∴ \lambda = 3, \lambda = 2$

We have two values of~$\lambda$.

$⇒ \mathop{∑}_{\lambda \in s} ( \lambda + 2{)}^{2} = \left($3 + 2\right)2 + \left($2 + 2\right)2$

$= 41$

Hence,~ $\mathop{∑}_{\lambda \in s} ( \lambda + 2{)}^{2} = 41

questions.q: Let $\overset{→}{OA} = \overset{→}{a}, \overset{→}{OB} = 12\overset{→}{a} + 4\overset{→}{b}$ and $\overset{→}{OC} = \overset{→}{b}$, where $O$ is the origin. If $S$ is the parallelogram with adjacent sides $OA$ and $OC$, then $\dfrac{areaofthequadrilateralOABC}{areaofS}$ is equal to _____
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Area of parallelogram, $S = | \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} |$

Area of quadrilateral = Area \left(∆ OAB\right) +$Area \left(∆ OBC\right)$

$= \dfrac{1}{2} { | \overset{→}{a} \times ( 12\overset{→}{a} + 4\overset{→}{b} ) | + | \overset{→}{b} \times ( 12\overset{→}{a} + 4\overset{→}{b} ) | }$

$= \dfrac{1}{2} { | 4\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} | + | 12\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{a} | }$

$= \dfrac{1}{2} { 4 | \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} | + 12 | \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} | }$

$= \dfrac{16}{2} | \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} |$

$= 8 | ( \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} ) |$

Ratio $= \dfrac{8 | ( \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} ) |}{| ( \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} ) |} = 8

$

questions.q: Let $\overset{→}{a} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$~and $\overset{→}{c} = 2\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$. Then the number of vectors $\overset{→}{b}$~such that $\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c} = \overset{→}{a}$~and \left|\overset{→}{b}\right| \in \left\{1, 2, \ldots , 10\right\}$ \text{ and } is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,& $\overset{→}{a} = i + j - k$~and~$\overset{→}{c} = 2i - 3j + 2k$

$\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c} = \overset{→}{a}$~and~\left|\overset{→}{b}\right| \in \left\{1, 2 \ldots \ldots 10\right\}$

$∵ \overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c} = \overset{→}{a}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{a}$~is perpendicular to~$\overset{→}{b}$~as well as~$\overset{→}{a}$~is perpendicular to~$\overset{→}{c}$~, so~$\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{c} = 0$~as they are perpendicular.

Now checking~$\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{c} = 2 - 3 - 2 = - 3 \ne 0$

This~$\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c} = \overset{→}{a}$~is not possible.

So, number~of vectors~$\overset{→}{b} = 0$

$

questions.q: If $\vec{a}$ is nonzero vector such that its projections on the vectors $2 \hat{i}-\hat{j}+2 \hat{k}, \hat{i}+2 \hat{j}-2 \hat{k}$ and $\hat{k}$ are equal, then a unit vector along $\vec{a}$ is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let $\overline{\mathrm{a}}=\mathrm{a}_1 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+\mathrm{a}_2 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+\mathrm{a}_3 \hat{\mathrm{k}}$
$\mathrm{a}_1^2+\mathrm{a}_2^2+\mathrm{a}_3^2=1$
Let $\overline{\mathrm{b}}=2 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{i}}-\hat{\mathrm{j}}+2 \hat{\mathrm{k}}, \overline{\mathrm{c}}=\overrightarrow{\mathrm{i}}-2 \hat{\mathrm{j}}-2 \hat{\mathrm{k}}$
$\overline{\mathrm{d}}=\hat{\mathrm{k}}$
$\frac{\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{b}}}{|\mathrm{b}|}=\frac{\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}}}{|\mathrm{c}|}=\frac{\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{d}}}{|\mathrm{d}|}$
$\frac{2 \mathrm{a}_1-\mathrm{a}_2+2 \mathrm{a}_3}{3}=\frac{\mathrm{a}_1+2 \mathrm{a}_2-2 \mathrm{a}_3}{3}=\mathrm{a}_3$
By solving
$\mathrm{a}_1=\frac{7}{\sqrt{155}}, \mathrm{a}_2=\frac{9}{\sqrt{155}}, \mathrm{a}_3=\frac{5}{\sqrt{155}}$

questions.q: Let $\overset{→}{a} = 3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{b} = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$ be two vectors. If a vector perpendicular to both the vectors $\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b}$ and $\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b}$ has the magnitude $12$ then one such vector is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\overset{→}{a} = 3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{b} = i + 2\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$
$∵ \overset{→}{\alpha} = \overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b} = 4\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j}$
$\overset{→}{\beta} = \overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b} = 2\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{k}$
$∴ \overset{→}{\alpha} \times \overset{→}{\beta} = \left|$\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 4 & 4 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 4\end{cases}$\right| = \overset{^}{i}\left(16\right) - \overset{^}{j}\left(16\right) + \overset{^}{k}\left(- 8\right) = 16\overset{^}{i} - 16\overset{^}{j} - 8\overset{^}{k}$
$∴$ Unit vector perpendicular to $\overset{→}{\alpha} \text{ and } \overset{→}{\beta}$ is
$\overset{^}{n} = \dfrac{\overset{→}{\alpha} \times \overset{→}{\beta}}{\left|\overset{→}{\alpha} \times \overset{→}{\beta}\right|} = \dfrac{2\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}}{3}$
$∴$ Required vector $= 12\dfrac{\left(2\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right)}{3} = 4 \left(2\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right)$

questions.q:
Let $ABC be a triangle such that $\overset{→}{BC} = \overset{→}{a}, \overset{→}{CA} = \overset{→}{b}$, $\overset{→}{AB} = \overset{→}{c}, \left|\overset{→}{a}\right| = 6\sqrt{2}, \left|\overset{→}{b}\right| = 2\sqrt{3} and $\overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{c} = 12$ Consider the statements :

\left(S1\right)$:~\left|\left(\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right) + \left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{b}\right)\right| - \left|\overset{→}{c}\right| =6 \lleft(2\sqrt{2} -1)$

\left(S2\right)$: $∠ ABC = \cos^{- 1} $\left(\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}).Then

$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We know that by triangle law of vector addition,

$\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{c} = 0$

$⇒ \overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{c} = - \overset{→}{a}$

Squaring both side we get,

\left|\overset{→}{b}\right|2 + \left|\overset{→}{c}\right|2 + 2\overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{c} = \left|\overset{→}{a}\right|2$

Now putting the given value~\left|\overset{→}{a}\right| = 6\sqrt{2}, \left|\overset{→}{b}\right| = 2\sqrt{3} \text{ and } \overset{→}{b} . \overset{→}{c} = 12$

We get,~\left|\overset{→}{c}\right|2 = 36$

So,~\left|\overset{→}{c}\right| = 6$

Now,~$S1: \left|\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{b}\right| - \left|\overset{→}{c}\right|$

$⇒ \left|\left(\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{c}\right) \times \overset{→}{b}\right| - \left|\overset{→}{c}\right|$

$⇒ 0 - 6 = - 6$

And~$S2: \overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{c} = 0$

$\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b} = - \overset{→}{c}$

Squaring both side we get,

\left|\overset{→}{a}\right|2 + \left|\overset{→}{b}\right|2 - 2\left|\overset{→}{a}\right|\left|\overset{→}{b}\right|\cos \left(∠ ACB\right) = \left|\overset{→}{c}\right|2$

$⇒ 72 + 12 - 24\sqrt{6}\cos \left(∠ ACB\right) = 36$

$⇒ \cos \left(∠ ACB\right) = \dfrac{48}{24\sqrt{6}} = \dfrac{2}{6} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}$

$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$A \left(1, 3, 2\right), B \left(-$2, 8, 0\right) & $C\left($3, 6, 7\right)$

And angle bisector of $∠ BAC$ meets the line $BC$ at $D$,

Now, plotting the diagram we get,

Now, finding

$\overset{→}{AC} = 2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{AC}\right| = \sqrt{4 + 9 + 25} = \sqrt{38}

And \left|\overset{→}{AB}\right| = \sqrt{9 + 25 + 4} = \sqrt{38}

Using angle bisector theorem, we get

\dfrac{BD}{CD} = \dfrac{AB}{AC}

$⇒ BD: CD = 1: 1$

Using section formula to find coordinates of $D$,

$⇒ D ≡ $\left(\dfrac{1 \times 3 + 1 \left(-2\right)}${1 + 2},\dfrac{1 \times 6 + 1 \times 8}{1 + 2}, \dfrac{1 \times 7 + 1 \times 0}{1 + 2})$

$⇒ D ≡ \left(\dfrac{1}{2},7, \dfrac{7}{2}\right)$

$⇒ \overset{→}{AD} = - \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{i} +4\overset{^}{j} + \dfrac{3}{2}\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{AD} = \dfrac{1}{2} \left(- \overset{^}{i} +8\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right)$

Length of projection of $\overset{→}{AD}$ on $\overset{→}{AC}$ is given by,

$⇒ d = \left|\overset{→}{AD} \cdot \overset{→}{AC}\overset{→}{AC}\right|$

$⇒ d = \dfrac{37}{2\sqrt{38}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given that&

$\dfrac{1}{8}\overset{→}{a}$~is a unit vector.

$| \overset{→}{a} | = 8$
$| 2\overset{→}{a} + 3\overset{→}{b}{|}^{2} = | 3\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b}{|}^{2}$

We know that$\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b} = \left|\overset{→}{a}\right|\left|\overset{→}{b}\right|cos\theta,$
$⇒ 4 | \overset{→}{a}{|}^{2} + 9 | \overset{→}{b}{|}^{2} + 12 | \overset{→}{a} | | \overset{→}{b} | \cos 60 ° = 9 | \overset{→}{a}{|}^{2} + | \overset{→}{b}{|}^{2} + 6 | \overset{→}{a} | | \overset{→}{b} | \cos 60 °$
$⇒ 5 | \overset{→}{a}{|}^{2} = 8 | \overset{→}{b}{|}^{2} + 6 | \overset{→}{a} | | | \overset{→}{b} ∣ \cos 60 °$
$⇒ 5\left(64\right) = 8 | \overset{→}{b}{|}^{2} + 6\left(8\right) \cdot | \overset{→}{b} | \dfrac{1}{2}$
\left⇒ | \overset{→}{b}{|}^{2} + 3 | \overset{→}{b} | - 40 = 0 ⇒ \left(\left|\overset{→}{b}\right| + 8\right) | \overset{→}{b} | - 5\right) = 0$
$⇒ | \overset{→}{b} | = 5$

$

questions.solution:
As, We know that& $\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} = \left|$\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 3 & 2 & x \\ 1 & - 1 & 1\end{cases}$\right|$
$= \left(2 + x\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(x - 3\right)\overset{^}{j} - 5\overset{^}{k}$

\left|\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right| = \sqrt{4 + x^{2} + 4x + x^{2} + 9 - 6x + 25}$

$= \sqrt{2x^{2} - 2x + 38}$

Therefore, we have
$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right| \ge \sqrt{\dfrac{75}{2}}$

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right| \ge 5\sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2}}$

$

questions.q: An arc $PQ$~of a circle subtends a right angle at its centre $O$. The mid point of the arc $PQ$ is $R$. If~$\overset{→}{OP} = \overset{→}{u}, \overset{→}{OR} = \overset{→}{v}$~and~$\overset{→}{OQ} = \alpha\overset{→}{u} + \beta\overset{→}{v}$, then~$\alpha, {β}^{2}$, are the roots of the equation
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

An arc $PQ$~of a circle subtends a right angle at its centre $O$. The mid point of the arc $PQ$ is $R$,

And~$\overset{→}{OP} = \overset{→}{u}, \overset{→}{OR} = \overset{→}{v}$~and~$\overset{→}{OQ} = \alpha\overset{→}{u} + \beta\overset{→}{v}$,~

So, plotting the diagram of the given value we get,

Now given,~$\overset{→}{OQ} = \alpha\overset{→}{u} + \beta\overset{→}{v}$

Where,~$\overset{→}{OR} = \overset{→}{v}$~and~$\overset{→}{OP} = \overset{→}{u}$

Now~\left|\overset{→}{OP}\right| = \left|\overset{→}{OQ}\right| = \text{radius}$, so~$R$~will lie on angle bisector of~$\overset{→}{OQ}$~and~$\overset{→}{OP}$

Now using the perpendicular condition we get,

$\overset{→}{OQ} \cdot \overset{→}{OP} = 0$

$⇒ \overset{→}{OQ} \cdot \overset{→}{OP} = \alpha\left|\overset{→}{u}\right|2 + \beta \cdot \left(\overset{→}{v} \cdot \overset{→}{u}\right) = 0$

$⇒ \alpha\left|\overset{→}{u}\right|2 + \beta \cdot \left(\left|\overset{→}{v}\right|\left|\overset{→}{u}\right|cos{45}^{°}\right) = 0$

$⇒ \alpha + \beta \cdot cos{45}^{°} = 0\left\{\text{as}\left|\overset{→}{u}\right| = \left|\overset{→}{v}\right| = \text{radius}\right\}$

$⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{- \beta}{2}$

Now solving,~$\overset{→}{OQ} \cdot \overset{→}{OR} = \left|\overset{→}{OQ}\right|\left|\overset{→}{OR}\right|cos{45}^{°} = \dfrac{1}{2}r^{2}$

$⇒ \left(\alpha\overset{→}{v} + \beta\overset{→}{v}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{→}{v}\right) = \dfrac{r2}{2}$

$⇒ \alpha \cdot \dfrac{r2}{2} + \beta \cdot r^{2} = \dfrac{r2}{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{α}{2} + \beta = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ \beta = \sqrt{2}$~\left\{\text{as}\alpha = \dfrac{- \beta}{2}\right\}$

So,~$\alpha = - 1$

Now finding the equation with roots~$\alpha = - 1, {β}^{2} = 2$~we get,~$x^{2} - x - 2 = 0$

questions.q: If a unit vector $\overset{→}{a}$ makes angles $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ with $\overset{^}{i}, \dfrac{π}{4}$~with $\overset{^}{j}$ and $\theta \in \left($0, $\pi\right) with $\overset{^}{k},$ then a value of \theta is:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The unit vector& $\overset{→}{a}$~makes angle~$\dfrac{π}{3}, \dfrac{π}{4}$~and~$\theta$~with~$\overset{^}{i}, \overset{^}{j} \text{ and } \overset{^}{k}$~respectively.

Hence, the direction cosines of the vector~$\overset{→}{a}$~are~$cos\alpha = cos\dfrac{π}{3} = \dfrac{1}{2}, cos\beta = cos\dfrac{π}{4} = \dfrac{1}{2}$~and~$cos\gamma = cos\theta$

For a line having direction cosines as~$cos\alpha, cos\beta, cos\gamma$

$⇒ \cos^{2}\alpha + \cos^{2}\beta + \cos^{2}\gamma = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{2} + \cos^{2}\theta = 1$

$⇒ \cos^{2}\theta = 1 - \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{1}{4}$

$⇒ \cos^{2}\theta = \pm \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ \theta = \dfrac{π}{3}$ or $\dfrac{2\pi}{3} .$
questions.question: If a unit vector $\overset{→}{a}$ makes angles $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ with $\overset{^}{i}, \dfrac{π}{4}$~with $\overset{^}{j}$ and $\theta \in \left($0, $\pi\right) with $\overset{^}{k},$ then a value of \theta is:$

questions.q: Let $\vec{a}=4 \hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}, \vec{b}=11 \hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ and $\vec{c}$ be a vector such that $(\vec{a}+\vec{b}) \times \vec{c}=\vec{c} \times(-2 \vec{a}+3 \vec{b})$. If $(2 \vec{a}+3 \vec{b}) \cdot \vec{c}=1670$, then $|\vec{c}|^2$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & (\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}) \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}-\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}} \times(-2 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}+3 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}})=0 \\ & (\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}) \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}+(-2 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}+3 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}) \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}=0 \\ & \Rightarrow(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}})-2 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}+3 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}) \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}=\lambda(4 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}-\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}) \\ & \Rightarrow=\lambda(44 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-4 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+4 \hat{\mathrm{k}}-4 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+\hat{\mathrm{j}}-\hat{\mathrm{k}}) \\ & =\lambda(40 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-3 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+3 \hat{\mathrm{k}})\end{aligned}$
Now
$\begin{aligned}
& (8 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-2 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+2 \hat{\mathrm{k}}+33 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-3 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+3 \hat{\mathrm{k}}) \cdot \lambda(40 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-3 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+3 \hat{\mathrm{k}})=1670 \\
& \Rightarrow(41 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-5 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+5 \hat{\mathrm{k}}) \cdot(40 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-3 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+3 \hat{\mathrm{k}}) \times \lambda=1670) \\
& \Rightarrow(1640+15+15) \lambda=1670 \Rightarrow \lambda=1 \\
& \text { so } \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}=40 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-3 \hat{\mathrm{j}}-3 \hat{\mathrm{k}} \\
& \Rightarrow|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}|^2=1600+9+9=1618
\end{aligned}$

$( \overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b} + ( \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} ) )$ and $\overset{→}{a}$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
| \overset{→}{a} | = | \overset{→}{b} | , | \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} | = | \overset{→}{a} | , \overset{→}{a} ⊥ \overset{→}{b}$

$| \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} | = | \overset{→}{a} | ⇒ | \overset{→}{a} | | \overset{→}{b} | \sin 90 ° = | \overset{→}{a} | ⇒ | \overset{→}{b} | = 1 = | \overset{→}{a} |$

$\overset{→}{a}$ and $\overset{→}{b}$ are mutually perpendicular unit~vectors.

$cos\theta = \dfrac{( \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k} ) \overset{^}{i}}{\sqrt{3}\sqrt{1}} = \dfrac{1}{3}⇒ \theta = \cos^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{1}{3})$

questions.q: Let the position vectors of three vertices of a triangle be $4 \vec{p}+\vec{q}-3 \vec{r},-5 \vec{p}+\vec{q}+2 \vec{r}$ and $2 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{p}}-\overrightarrow{\mathrm{q}}+2 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}}$. If the position vectors of the orthocenter and the circumcenter of the triangle are $\frac{\vec{p}+\vec{q}+\vec{r}}{4}$ and $\alpha \vec{p}+\beta \vec{q}+\gamma \vec{r}$ respectively, then $\alpha+2 \beta+5 \gamma$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We know that
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{O}\text { (orthocentre) } \frac{\overrightarrow{\mathrm{p}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{q}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}}}{4} \\ & \mathrm{C}(\text { circum centre) } \alpha \overrightarrow{\mathrm{p}}+\beta \overrightarrow{\mathrm{q}}+\gamma \overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}} \\ & \mathrm{C} \text { (centroid) }=\frac{\overrightarrow{\mathrm{p}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{q}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}}}{3} \end{aligned}$ by relation $\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 2(\alpha \overrightarrow{\mathrm{p}}+\beta \overrightarrow{\mathrm{q}}+\gamma \overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}})+\frac{\overrightarrow{\mathrm{p}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{q}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}}}{4}=3\left(\frac{\overrightarrow{\mathrm{p}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{q}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}}}{3}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow 8(\alpha \overrightarrow{\mathrm{p}}+\beta \overrightarrow{\mathrm{q}}+\gamma \overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}})=3(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{p}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{q}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}}) \\ & \Rightarrow 8 \alpha=3,8 \beta=3,8 \gamma=3 \\ & \alpha=\frac{3}{8}, \beta=\frac{3}{8}, \gamma=\frac{3}{8} \\ & \therefore \alpha+2 \beta+3 \gamma \\ & \frac{3}{8}+\frac{6}{8}+\frac{15}{8}=\frac{24}{8}=3 \end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $\overset{→}{a} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{b} = 2\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$~and $\overset{→}{c} = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$~be the three given vectors. Let $\overset{→}{v}$~be a vector in~the plane of $\overset{→}{a}$~and $\overset{→}{b}$~whose projection on $\overset{→}{c}$~is $\dfrac{2}{3}$. If $\overset{→}{v}, \overset{^}{j} = 7$, then $\overset{→}{v} \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}\right) \text{ and } is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Since vector& $\overset{→}{v}, \overset{→}{a} \text{ and } \overset{→}{b}$~are coplanar then, $\overset{→}{v} = {λ}_{1}\overset{→}{a} + {λ}_{2}\overset{→}{b}$, where ${λ}_{1}, {λ}_{2} \in \mathbb{R}$.

$⇒ \overset{→}{v} = \left({λ}_{1} + 2{λ}_{2}\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left({λ}_{1} - 3{λ}_{2}\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(2{λ}_{1} + {λ}_{2}\right)\overset{^}{k}$

$∵$ Projection of $\overset{→}{v}$ on $\overset{→}{c}$~is $\dfrac{2}{3}$

$∴ \dfrac{{λ}_{1} + 2{λ}_{2} - {λ}_{1} + 3{λ}_{2} + 2{λ}_{1} + {λ}_{2}}{3} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

$∴ {λ}_{1} + 3{λ}_{2} = 1 . . . \left(1\right)$

and $\overset{→}{v} \cdot \overset{^}{j} =7 ⇒ {λ}_{1} - 3{λ}_{2} = 7 . . . \left(2\right)$

$⇒ \overset{→}{v} = \left({λ}_{1} +2{λ}_{2}\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left({λ}_{1} -3{λ}_{2}\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(2{λ}_{1} + {λ}_{2}\right)\overset{^}{k}$

$∴ {λ}_{1} + 3{λ}_{2} = 1 . . . \left(1\right)$

$⇒ {λ}_{1} - 3{λ}_{2} = 7 \left($2\right)$
From equation \left($1\right)$ and \left($2\right)$, we get

${λ}_{1} = 4, {λ}_{2} = - 1$

$∴ \overset{→}{v} = 2\overset{^}{i} + 7\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k}$

$∴ \overset{→}{v} $\cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}\right) =$2 + 7 = 9$

$

questions.q: Let $PQR$be a triangle. The points$A, B$ and $C$ are on the sides $QR, RP$ and~$PQ$ respectively such that~$\dfrac{QA}{AR} = \dfrac{RB}{BP} = \dfrac{PC}{CQ} = \dfrac{1}{2}$. Then~$\dfrac{Area\left(∆ PQR\right)}{Area\left(∆ ABC\right)}$& is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let the position vector of& $P$~is~$\overset{→}{O}$,~$Q$~is~$\overset{→}{q}$~and~$R$~is~$\overset{→}{r}$.

Now,~position vector of~$A$~is

$\dfrac{2\overset{→}{q} + \overset{→}{r}}{3}$

Position vector of~$B$~is~$\dfrac{2\overset{→}{r}}{3}$.

Position vector of~$C$~is~$\overset{→}{q}3$.

$\overset{→}{AB} = \dfrac{\overset{→}{r} - 2\overset{→}{q}}{3}$

$\overset{→}{AC} = \dfrac{- \overset{→}{r} - \overset{→}{q}}{3}$

So,

$\overset{→}{AB} \times \overset{→}{AC} = \dfrac{1}{3}\left[\left(\overset{→}{r} - 2\overset{→}{q}\right) \times \left(- \overset{→}{r} - \overset{→}{q}\right)\right]

$⇒ \overset{→}{AB} $\times \overset{→}{AC} = \dfrac{1}{3}\left[- \left(\overset{→}{r} \times \overset{→}{q}\right) +$2 \left(\overset{→}{q} \times \overset{→}{r}\right)\right]$

$⇒ \overset{→}{AB} \times \overset{→}{AC} = \left(\overset{→}{q} \times \overset{→}{r}\right)

Area of~$∆ PQR$~is~=\dfrac{1}{2}\left|\overset{→}{q} \times \overset{→}{r}\right|

Area of~$∆ ABC$~is~\dfrac{1}{2}\left|\overset{→}{AB} \times \overset{→}{AC}\right|

Area of~$∆ ABC = $\dfrac{1}{2}\left|\overset{→}{q} \times \overset{→}{r}\right|

Therefore,

\dfrac{Area\left(∆ PQR\right)}{Area\left(∆ ABC\right)} =$1

$

questions.q: Let $\overset{→}{a}$~be a vector which is perpendicular to the vector $3\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$. If $\overset{→}{a} \times \left(2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}\right) = 2\overset{^}{i} - 13\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}$, then the projection of the vector $\overset{→}{a}$~on the vector $2\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$& is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,& $\overset{→}{a} \times \left(2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}\right) = 2\overset{^}{i} - 13\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}$

Now multiplying both side by~ \left(3\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right)$~we get,

$⇒ \left(\overset{→}{a} \times \left(2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}\right)\right) \times \left(3\overset{^}{i} + $\dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{j} +$2\overset{^}{k}\right)$

$= \left(2\overset{^}{i} - 13\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}\right) \times \left(3\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right)$

$⇒ \left(\left(3\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right) . \overset{→}{a}\right)\left(2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}\right) - \left(6 + 2\right)\overset{→}{a} = \left|$\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 2 & - 13 & - 4 \\ 3 & \dfrac{1}{2} & 2\end{cases}$\right|$

$⇒ 0 - \left(6 + 2\right)\overset{→}{a} = \left|$\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 2 & - 13 & - 4 \\ 3 & \dfrac{1}{2} & 2\end{cases}$\right|$

$\overset{→}{a} = 3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 5\overset{^}{k}$

Now, projection of~$\overset{→}{a}$~on vector~$2\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$~is~$\overset{→}{a} \cdot \left(2\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)3 = \dfrac{5}{3}$

$

questions.q: Let $\overset{→}{a}, \overset{→}{b}$ and $\overset{→}{c}$ be three vectors such that \left|\overset{→}{a}\right| = \sqrt{3}, \left|\overset{→}{b}\right| = 5, \overset{→}{b} ∙ \overset{→}{c} = 10$ and the angle between $\overset{→}{b}$ and $\overset{→}{c}$ is $\dfrac{\pi}{3} .$ If $\overset{→}{a}$ is perpendicular to the vector $\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c},$ then \left|\overset{→}{a} \times \left(\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c}\right)\right|$ is equal to ____________.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\overset{→}{b} . \overset{→}{c} = 10 ⇒ \left|\overset{→}{b}\right|\left|\overset{→}{c}\right|\cos \left(\dfrac{π}{3}\right) = 10 ⇒ 5 . \left|\overset{→}{c}\right| . \dfrac{1}{2} = 10$

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{c}\right| = 4$

Also, $\overset{→}{a} . \left(\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c}\right) = 0$

\left|\overset{→}{a} \times \left(\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c}\right)\right| = \left|\overset{→}{a}\right| \left|\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c}\right|$\sin \left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right)

$⇒ $\sqrt{3} \times \left|\overset{→}{b}\right|\left|\overset{→}{c}\right|$sin $\dfrac{π}{3} \times$1$

$⇒ $\sqrt{3} \times$5 $\times$4 $\times \dfrac{3}{2} =$30$

$

questions.q: Let $\overset{→}{a}, \overset{→}{b}, \overset{→}{c}$ be three mutually perpendicular vectors of the same magnitude and equally inclined at an angle $\theta$, with the vector $\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{c}$. Then $36\cos^{2}2\theta$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,

\left|\overset{→}{a}\right| = \left|\overset{→}{b}\right| = \left|\overset{→}{c}\right|$

$\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b} = \overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{c} = \overset{→}{c} \cdot \overset{→}{a} = 0$

Since, vectors are mutually perpendicular and of equally magnitude, hence let

$\overset{→}{a} = \overset{^}{i}, \overset{→}{b} = \overset{^}{j}, \overset{→}{c} = \overset{^}{k}$

Now,

\left(\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{c}\right) \cdot \overset{→}{a} = \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \overset{^}{i}$

$⇒ \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \overset{^}{i} = \sqrt{3} \cdot 1 \cdot cos\theta$

$⇒ 1 + 0 + 0 = \sqrt{3} \cdot 1 \cdot cos\theta$

$⇒ \sqrt{3}cos\theta = 1$

$⇒ cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{3}$

$⇒ \cos 2\theta = 2\cos^{2}\theta - 1 = \dfrac{2}{3} - 1$

$⇒ \cos 2\theta = - \dfrac{1}{3}$

$⇒ \cos^{2}2\theta = \dfrac{1}{9}$

$⇒ 36\cos^{2}2\theta = 4$

questions.q: Let $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}=\hat{i}-3 \hat{j}+7 \hat{k}, \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}=2 \hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}$ be a vector such that $(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}+2 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}) \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}=3(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}})$. If $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c}=130$, then $\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}$ is equal to _______
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & (\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}+2 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}) \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}=3(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}) \\ & (2 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}+4 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}) \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}=0 \\ & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}=\lambda(4 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}+2 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}})=\lambda(8 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-14 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+30 \hat{\mathrm{k}}) \\ & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}=130 \\ & 8 \lambda+42 \lambda+210 \lambda=130 \\ & \lambda=\frac{1}{2} \\ & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}=4 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-7 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+15 \hat{\mathrm{k}} \\ & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}=8+7+15=30\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If & $\overset{→}{a}$ and $\overset{→}{b}$~are unit vectors and~  \left(\overset{→}{a} + 3\overset{→}{b}\right)$ is perpendicular to~  \left(7\overset{→}{a} - 5\overset{→}{b}\right)$ and~  \left(\overset{→}{a} - 4\overset{→}{b}\right)$ is perpendicular to~\left(7\overset{→}{a} - 2\overset{→}{b}\right),$~then the angle between~$\overset{→}{a}$ and $\overset{→}{b} (in degrees) is _________.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,& \left(\overset{→}{a} + 3\overset{→}{b}\right) ⊥ \left(7\overset{→}{a} - 5\overset{→}{b}\right)$

Therefore,~ \left(\overset{→}{a} +$3\overset{→}{b}\right)\cdot \left($7\overset{→}{a} - 5\overset{→}{b}\right) = 0$

$⇒ $7\left|\overset{→}{a}\right|$2 - 15 \left|\overset{→}{b}\right|2 + 16\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b} =0 \ldots \left(1\right)$

and~ \left(\overset{→}{a} -$4\overset{→}{b}\right)$\cdot \left($7\overset{→}{a} - 2\overset{→}{b}\right) = 0$

$⇒ $7\left|\overset{→}{a}\right|$2 + 8 \left|\overset{→}{b}\right|2 - 30\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b} =0 \ldots \left(2\right)$

From \left(1\right)$ and \left(2\right),$~we get

$2\left|\overset{→}{a}\right|cos\theta = \left|\overset{→}{b}\right|$

$∴ cos\theta = \left|\overset{→}{b}\right|2\left|\overset{→}{a}\right|$

$⇒ \theta =60 ° .

$

questions.q: Let $\overset{→}{a}, \overset{→}{b}, \overset{→}{c}$ be three vectors such that \left|\overset{→}{a}\right| = \sqrt{31}, 4\left|\overset{→}{b}\right| = \left|\overset{→}{c}\right| = 2$ and $2\left(\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right) = 3 \left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{a}\right). If the angle between $\overset{→}{b}$ and $\overset{→}{c}$ is \dfrac{2\pi}{3}, then \left(\dfrac{\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{c}}{\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}}\right)$2$& is equal to _____ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

\left|\overset{→}{a}\right| = \sqrt{31}, 4\left|\overset{→}{b}\right| = \left|\overset{→}{c}\right| = 2$,~$2\left(\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right) = 3 \left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{a}\right)~and angle between~$\overset{→}{b} \text{ and } \overset{→}{c}$~is given as~\dfrac{2\pi}{3}

Now solving,~$3\left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{a}\right) +$2\left(\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{a}\right) =$0$

$⇒ \left($3\overset{→}{c} $\times$2\overset{→}{b}\right)$\times \overset{→}{a} =$0$

Means~\left($3\overset{→}{c} $\times$2\overset{→}{b}\right) \text{ and } \overset{→}{a}$~are parallel vector,

So, let~$3\overset{→}{c} $\times$2\overset{→}{b} = \lambda\overset{→}{a}$

Now squaring both sides we get,
$9\left|\overset{→}{c}\right|$2 + 4\left|\overset{→}{b}\right|$2 + 12\left(\overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{c}\right) = {λ}^{2}\left|\overset{→}{a}\right|$2$

$⇒ 36 + 1 + 12 $\times \dfrac{1}{2} \times$2 \left(cos \lleft(2\dfrac{π}{3}\right)) = {λ}^{2}\left(31\right)$

$⇒ {λ}^{2} = 1$

$⇒ \lambda = \pm1$

Now putting the value of~$\lambda$~in~\left(3\overset{→}{c} \times2\overset{→}{b}\right) = \lambda\overset{→}{a}$~we get,

$3\overset{→}{c} + 2\overset{→}{b} = \pm \overset{→}{a} \ldots \left(1\right)$

Now taking dot product~with~$\overset{→}{b}$~in above equation we get,

$3\left(\overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{c}\right) + 2\left(\overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{b}\right) = \pm \overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b} = \pm \left(- \dfrac{3}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \pm \left(-1\right)$

$⇒ \left(\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}\right)2 = 1$

Again taking~$3\left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{a}\right) =2 \left(\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right)~and sqauring both side,

$⇒ \left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{a}\right)$2 = $\dfrac{4}{9} \left(\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right)$2$

$⇒ \left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{a}\right)$2 = \dfrac{4}{9}\left[\left|\overset{→}{a}\right|2 \left|\overset{→}{b}\right|$2 - \left(\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}\right)2\right]$

$⇒ \left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{a}\right)2 = $\dfrac{4}{9}\left[\dfrac{31}{4} - \left($1\right)\right]$

$⇒ \left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{a}\right)$2 = \dfrac{4}{9} \times \dfrac{27}{4} =3$

Hence, the value of~\left(\dfrac{\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{c}}{\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}})2 = \dfrac{3}{1} =3$.

$
